summary: Phase 4 test specifications for the so-mo-linkage contract. 31 Playwright specs (8 fast + 23 slow) mapped 1:1 to Phase 3 scenarios. All specs use the existing repo conventions: test/e2e/fixtures.ts (custom test + db fixture, RLS-scoped Drizzle proxy), test/helpers/api.ts (testFetch + domain helpers), describe-level shared state for serial stories, Date.now() suffixes for collision-free names, parseFloat() on numeric strings, and Promise.allSettled for concurrent scenarios. REVISION CORRECTIONS: (1) DB column corrections — items table has NO expectedQty/committedQty/onHandQty/demandQty; those live on inventoryItemBalances (lib/db/schema/inventory-projections.ts:91-110), keyed by (organizationId, locationId, itemId); specs SUM these across locations. (2) salesOrders has NO cancelledAt column (lib/db/schema/sales.ts:31); a conceptually 'cancelled' SO = deletedAt IS NOT NULL. (3) testFetch idempotency mechanic — the auto-key is `${operationName}:${randomUUID()}` per call (lib/api/idempotency-client.ts:8); identical bodies get DISTINCT keys, so there is NO auto-replay-on-same-body. Same-key replay (S17/S18/S19) requires explicit options.headers['Idempotency-Key']. Two new spec files: test/e2e/fast/so-mo-linkage.spec.ts (8 specs) and test/e2e/slow/so-mo-linkage.spec.ts (23 specs, serial mode). The slow file groups describe blocks by risk_category. S29 is flagged experimental — it pins a confirmed production code defect (validateSalesLineLinkInTx has no existing_active_mo check at queries.ts:729-819); the spec asserts the current 'BR-1 violated via PUT' outcome and will fail loudly if a fix lands, forcing a contract update. S15 and S24 carry the same gap on the POST path (T24 modelled outcome). All concurrency specs use Promise.allSettled and identify winner/loser by response shape.

inferences.claim: testFetch's automatic Idempotency-Key fingerprint means specs that retry the SAME body (S17 replay, S22 dead-write replay) will get the SAME key automatically — but specs that fire two DIFFERENT requests intending the same key, or specs that want NO key at all, must override headers explicitly. Phase 5 must therefore use options.headers to either (a) set an explicit shared key for forced-replay tests, (b) vary the key with a counter, OR (c) for S15/S24 'no-key duplicate POST', either rely on testFetch's deterministic fingerprint (which means S15 effectively tests 'same-key replay' rather than 'no-key duplicate') — OR pass a custom http request that omits createIdempotencyHeaders.

For S15 and S24, the modelled outcome (T24: two distinct MO rows, both 201) requires DIFFERENT idempotency keys per request. testFetch's default behavior already provides distinct randomUUID-suffixed keys per call, so explicit headers are optional for correctness — but Phase 5 should pass explicit headers (e.g. `t24-${i}`) for documentation and to make the test intent unambiguous. This exercises the 'no shared key, no existing_active_mo guard' code path.

repo_patterns.fixture_shape: Custom `test` from test/e2e/fixtures.ts exposes `db` (RLS-scoped Drizzle proxy via Proxy on `appDb` with set_config('app.current_org_id') per query) and `page` (Playwright Page with auto-injected test session cookie). repo_patterns.auth_pattern: All requests authenticate via the canonical test user session cookie injected into every browser context by the fixture. testFetch() includes the cookie automatically; do NOT manually attach headers. Secondary users (S14 only) use the invite-and-join pattern from test/e2e/team-management.spec.ts:672+ — launch a fresh browser context with a new session cookie.
repo_patterns.api_helpers: test/helpers/api.ts exports: testFetch (low-level), createCustomer, createItem, updateItem, deleteItem, createUnit, createSalesOrder, updateSalesOrder, confirmSalesOrder, fulfillSalesOrder, createManufacturingOrder, releaseManufacturingOrder, completeManufacturingOrder, createPurchaseOrder, submitPurchaseOrder, receivePurchaseOrder, getOrgId, getUnitId, getBaseUrl, getSessionCookie. Each domain helper returns { status, body }. Use these over inline fetch calls.
repo_patterns.idempotency_helper: CORRECTED in revision: test/helpers/api.ts testFetch() auto-applies createIdempotencyHeaders() for any non-GET/HEAD method when the caller has NOT supplied Idempotency-Key. The actual key is `${operationName}:${randomUUID()}` (per lib/api/idempotency-client.ts:8). The body sha256 only namespaces the operationName; the unique key part is a per-call randomUUID. So distinct testFetch calls with identical bodies STILL get DISTINCT keys — there is no auto-replay-on-same-body. Implications for tests: (a) For SAME-KEY replay (S17 SO confirm replay, S18 bulk-confirm replay, S19 MO complete replay): the spec MUST explicitly set options.headers['Idempotency-Key']='K1' on BOTH calls. (b) For DISTINCT-KEY parallel (S15 single-create race, S24 cross-endpoint race): the default testFetch behavior already gives distinct keys; no override needed, but document the intent. (c) createIdempotencyHeaders preserves caller-supplied keys (only sets when absent), so options.headers['Idempotency-Key']='K1' is the standard override mechanism — no raw fetch needed.
repo_patterns.db_assertion_pattern: Domain tables imported from '../../../lib/db/schema' (relative from test/e2e/slow|fast). Use drizzle-orm helpers: eq, and, sql, inArray, isNull. Numeric columns return strings (e.g. '5.0000'); convert with parseFloat before arithmetic comparisons. Use trimScale via raw string comparison or parseFloat(...).toFixed(4) when comparing exact deltas.
repo_patterns.shared_state_pattern: test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial' }) for files where tests depend on each other; share state via describe-level let/const variables, not via global helper functions. Each test file should be self-contained — never import shared helpers from another spec file.
repo_patterns.naming_convention: All created entities suffix names with Date.now() (e.g. `Linked MO Material ${ts}`). SKUs follow the form `MAT-NAME-${ts}` / `PROD-NAME-${ts}`. Customer names follow `Linked MO Customer ${ts}`. Avoid cross-spec name collisions even when serial.
repo_patterns.concurrent_pattern: Promise.allSettled for parallel races. Identify winner/loser by response shape (status, body.created.length, body.error) rather than by Promise resolution order — lock acquisition order is undefined under PG FOR UPDATE.
repo_patterns.page_object_pattern: No page-object classes. Page interactions use page.getByRole / getByLabel / getByPlaceholder / locator() directly inside each test. Form helpers (filterList, selectDate, getIdFromUrl) live in test/e2e/fixtures.ts.
repo_patterns.common_setup_steps: 1. const ts = Date.now(); 2. const unitId = getUnitId(); 3. createItem(material) → seeded stock auto-creates a lot; 4. createItem(product, { bom: [...] }) seeds the active BOM revision; 5. createCustomer(name) returns id; 6. createSalesOrder({ customerId, lines: [...] }) returns SO id; 7. createManufacturingOrder({ productId, salesOrderId, salesOrderLineId, ingredients }) returns MO id; 8. read sales order line id via `db.select().from(salesOrderLines).where(eq(salesOrderLines.salesOrderId, soId))`.
repo_patterns.lane_assignment_rule: Fast: ≤60s, single-write, no role-switching, no concurrent retries (8 specs). Slow: serial story, multi-step setup, cross-route navigation, idempotency replay, concurrent races (23 specs).

test_specs.test_name: item soft-delete succeeds when item is referenced only by a cancelled MO (deletedAt SET): T26 inverse

test_specs.test_name: parallel PUT update and DELETE on the same MO serialize without ingredient orphans; final state is self-consistent
test_specs.purpose: Pin the row-lock invariant for same-MO PUT vs DELETE: both paths use FOR UPDATE on the MO row, so they serialize. Final state: exactly one row exists; either deletedAt SET (delete won) or PUT's changes applied (update won); never both.

seed_data: Customer + product + raw material + open SO + sales-linked MO in MO_ACTIVE (no picks)

interaction_plan: Construct PUT payload with a notes change (NOTES_NEW).

Issue both in parallel via Promise.allSettled with explicit distinct Idempotency-Keys: testFetch(`/api/manufacturing-orders/${moId}`, { method: 'PUT', body: JSON.stringify(updateBody), headers }) AND testFetch(`/api/manufacturing-orders/${moId}`, { method: 'DELETE', headers }).
Read both response statuses + bodies.
Query MO row state from DB to determine outcome (the explicit DB-state discriminator): SELECT id, deletedAt, notes FROM manufacturingOrders WHERE id=$moId. The row state determines which path 'won':
- deletedAt IS NOT NULL AND notes != NOTES_NEW → DELETE won (PUT either lost the race or saw the deleted row)
- deletedAt IS NULL AND notes = NOTES_NEW → PUT won, DELETE either failed or was queued
- deletedAt IS NOT NULL AND notes = NOTES_NEW → BOTH applied (PUT first, then DELETE); acceptable serial outcome
- deletedAt IS NULL AND notes != NOTES_NEW → neither applied (impossible if at least one returned 200; would indicate test bug or DB rollback)

behavioral: Exactly one of PUT/DELETE returns 200; the other returns either 404 (delete won, PUT sees no row) OR 200 (both succeed serially with delete second) OR 400 (state-changed)
Both responses cannot both fail with 5xx (that would indicate corruption)
Phase 5 must classify the outcome by reading DB row state (per interaction_plan steps 4-8) and assert exactly one of the three valid combinations
side_effects: Exactly one manufacturingOrders row exists for the MO id (no duplicate)
If deletedAt IS NOT NULL: cancellation side-effects are present (allocations cancelled); salesOrders has no separate cancelledAt column
If deletedAt IS NULL: PUT's NOTES_NEW is persisted in manufacturingOrders.notes
Never the impossible combo: deletedAt IS NULL AND notes != NOTES_NEW (would indicate both writes were rolled back — corruption)
negative_assertions: No ingredient orphans (manufacturingOrderIngredients rows with no matching MO)

flakiness_risks: Lock acquisition order is undefined — assertions must be by post-state, not by Promise resolution order

test_specs.test_name: PUT /api/manufacturing-orders/[id] is naturally idempotent on retry: ingredient demand and allocations end in the same state
test_specs.purpose: Pin the retry semantics for MO PUT (no requireIdempotencyKey): same body submitted twice produces the same net inventory state — no duplicate ingredient rows, no duplicate active allocations, two cancelled allocations in the audit trail.

seed_data: Customer + product + raw material + open SO + sales-linked MO in MO_ACTIVE (no picks)

interaction_plan: Capture initial state: manufacturingOrderIngredients rows (count + itemIds); SUM(inventoryItemBalances.expectedQty) for product across locations; stockAllocations active rows WHERE demandType='manufacturing_order_ingredient' for each ingredient.
PUT /api/manufacturing-orders/<mo> with the original body + a notes field — first call.

PUT /api/manufacturing-orders/<mo> with the SAME body again — second call. testFetch's default already produces a distinct randomUUID-suffixed key per call; the second PUT inherently sees a different key. The test asserts natural-idempotency of the PUT path (same net DB state) despite the absence of requireIdempotencyKey on this route.
Read final state.

behavioral: Both PUTs return 200
Response bodies need not be byte-identical (ingredient row ids may differ; update hard-deletes + re-inserts)
side_effects: manufacturingOrderIngredients count for the MO equals the body's ingredient count exactly (no duplicates)
parseFloat(SUM(inventoryItemBalances.expectedQty)) for product unchanged from single-PUT expectation
stockAllocations active rows for each ingredient: exactly one active row per ingredient (the second PUT cancelled the first's and re-issued)
stockAllocations cancelled rows for each ingredient: exactly TWO (one per PUT) — audit trail preserved
negative_assertions: Never two active stockAllocations rows for the same ingredient

flakiness_risks: Phase 5 should pass distinct Idempotency-Keys explicitly so the test asserts natural-idempotency of the PUT route — not idempotency-key-driven replay. testFetch's default randomUUID would also satisfy this, but explicit keys make the test intent clear

test_specs.test_name: moveReplacedSalesLineAllocationsInTx preserves allocations when SO has multiple same-itemId lines and is rewritten
test_specs.purpose: Pin moveReplacedSalesLineAllocationsInTx's pairing strategy: itemId + sortOrder via per-itemId bucket .shift(). Multi-line same-itemId rewrite must migrate active allocations from old line ids to new line ids in sortOrder order; no allocation references a deleted old line id.

Open SO with two lines for Product-A: line0 qty 5 sortOrder 0, line1 qty 3 sortOrder 1; CONFIRM both lines so each has an active stockAllocations row (demandType='sales_order_line')

interaction_plan: Capture pre-state: SELECT id, sortOrder FROM salesOrderLines WHERE salesOrderId=$soId ORDER BY sortOrder; SELECT id, demandId, createdAt FROM stockAllocations WHERE demandType='sales_order_line' AND demandId IN (line0, line1) AND status='active'.
PUT /api/sales-orders/<soId> with three Product-A lines: line0' qty 4 sortOrder 0, line1' qty 2 sortOrder 1, line2' qty 6 sortOrder 2.
Read post-state: salesOrderLines (should have 3 new ids), stockAllocations active rows.

behavioral: PUT returns 200
side_effects: Three new salesOrderLines rows exist for the SO (line0', line1', line2')
Old line0 and line1 ids are gone from salesOrderLines
stockAllocations active rows for demandId=line0' AND demandId=line1' exist (migrated from line0/line1 in sortOrder order)
line2' has its own fresh active allocation row (NOT a migration — distinguishable by createdAt timestamp later than line0'/line1')
No active stockAllocations row references line0 or line1 (the deleted ids)
negative_assertions: No active allocation row references an old (deleted) line id
Migration is by sortOrder pairing, not random — line0's allocation lands on line0', NOT on line1'

flakiness_risks: Distinguishing migrated vs fresh allocations may require comparing createdAt timestamps OR exact allocation id continuity — Phase 5 should compute the expected migration by ts pairing
